αἴαντός: Αἴας — Ajax, the Greek hero; masc. gen. sg.
βόε: βοῦς — ox, cow; masc. nom./acc. dual: ’the two oxen’ (as subject of a dual verb)
δέδηε: δαίω — kindle, burn; perf. 3 sg. intrans., epic: ‘is ablaze, burns’
θωὴν: θωή — a fine, penalty; acc. sg.
κάλει: καλέω — call, summon; impf. 3 sg., unaugmented (= ἐκάλει)
κατακτὰς: κατακτείνω — kill, slay; aor. 2 part. act. masc. nom. sg., stem κτα- (= Attic κατακτανών): ’having killed’
κεράεσσι: κέρας — horn; neut. dat. pl., epic -εσσι (= Attic κέρασι)
μάντιος: Μάντιος — Mantius, son of Melampus; masc. nom. sg.
μίμνει: μίμνω — stay, remain, wait; pres. 3 sg., epic reduplicated by-form of μένω
νειῷ: νειός — fallow field; fem. dat. sg. (νειῷ ἔνι τριπόλῳ ’in a thrice-ploughed fallow field’)
νούσῳ: νοῦσος (Attic νόσος) — sickness, disease; fem. dat. sg.
οἴνοπε: οἴνοψ — wine-faced, having the look of wine (the colour meant is unsettled); adj., masc. nom./acc. dual
στυγερήν: στυγερός — hateful, loathsome; fem. acc. sg., Ionic -ην (= Attic -άν)
χαλκήρεας: χαλκήρης — fitted with bronze; masc. acc. pl.
χθιζὸν: χθιζός — of yesterday; neut. acc. sg. used adverbially: ’yesterday’
ἀλέεινεν: ἀλεείνω — avoid, shun, evade; impf. 3 sg., unaugmented (Attic would lengthen to η-): ’evaded’
ἀνέγνω: ἀναγιγνώσκω — know for certain, recognise; aor. 3 sg., augment inside the compound (ἀν-έ-γνω), gnomic · also an ordinary narrative aor., not gnomic: ’recognised’ (νόον … ἀνέγνω ’recognised the mind’)
ἀπήμονες: ἀπήμων — unharmed, unscathed, safe; adj., masc. nom. pl.
ἔλθωμεν: ἔρχομαι — go, come; aor. subj. 1 pl.: ’we may come’ · also hortatory aor. subj. 1 pl. in a main clause: ’let us go’ (ἔλθωμεν δ’ ἀνὰ ἄστυ ’and let us go through the town’)
ἕταροι: ἑταῖρος — companion, comrade; masc. nom. pl., epic by-form ἕταροι (= ἑταῖροι)
ἱεμένω: ἵεμαι — be eager, strain forward, be impatient; pres. part. masc. dual: ’(though) eager, straining forward’
ἱπποδασείας: ἱπποδασύς — thick with horsehair; adj., fem. acc. pl., agreeing with κυνέας
ὀλοὴν: ὀλοός — deadly, destructive; fem. acc. sg.
ὦλκα: ὦλξ (ὄλκος) — furrow; masc. acc. sg., epic (cf. Attic αὖλαξ): ’furrow’
